authors: Roberto Ria\~no, Gorka Abad, Stjepan Picek, Aitor Urbieta
abstract: ArXiv:2607.28075v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Backdoor attacks on Spiking Neural Networks (SNNs) have primarily assumed dirty-label poisoning, in which triggered training samples are relabeled to an attacker-selected class. We study clean-label temporal poisoning, where a fixed timestamp transformation is applied only to the target-class training streams, leaving their labels unchanged. The transformation preserves the per-pixel, per-polarity event count exactly, making clean and triggered samples identical after temporal aggregation while altering the sequence processed by the SNN. Across three neuromorphic datasets and both convolutional and transformer-based victims, the attack reaches an ASR of 1.00 in the strongest configurations. We analyze the attack through poison-budget and trigger-shape ablations and evaluate established backdoor defenses adapted to spiking models. Defenses that collapse the time axis before inspection are blind by construction, while feature-space methods detect the poison only in selected settings. Our model-free detector, based on per-step event mass, detects the evaluated temporal transformations, demonstrating both the limitation of rate-collapsed defenses and the boundary of the attack's stealth. To our knowledge, this is the first clean-label backdoor attack evaluated on SNNs and neuromorphic event data.
tldr: This paper introduces a clean-label backdoor attack on spiking neural networks via temporal event redistribution, achieving high attack success rates on neuromorphic data.
motivation: The authors aim to demonstrate that SNNs are vulnerable to backdoor attacks even without label corruption, which is a novel threat model in neuromorphic computing.
method: They apply a fixed timestamp transformation to target-class training streams, preserving event counts but altering temporal order, and evaluate the attack on convolutional and transformer-based SNNs.
result: The attack achieves an ASR of 1.00 in strongest configurations, and defenses that collapse time are blind, while feature-space methods detect it only in some settings.
conclusion: The work highlights the need for temporal-aware defenses in SNNs and introduces a model-free detector based on per-step event mass.

title: Checking Information Flow In Cloud-based IoT Access Control Policies (Extended Version)
authors: Lorenzo Ceragioli, Letterio Galletta, Edoardo Lunati
abstract: ArXiv:2607.28088v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Many cloud providers for IoT technologies offer access control mechanisms whose proper configuration is critical for security. However, verifying permissions in isolation is insufficient in a setting where devices have different levels of trust or are compartmentalised in various subsystems. This work analyses IoT access control policies to identify potential security vulnerabilities from unwanted information flow between devices. To this end, we formally model AWS IoT Core's components and define an information flow graph to capture the communication among devices permitted by the access control policies. We build a finite representation of the graph by leveraging an SMT solver, thus enabling the verification of information flow between devices. We implement our approach in a tool called IOT:POKER, and assess it on a realistic scenario and several real-world policies.
tldr: This paper analyzes IoT access control policies for unwanted information flow using formal modeling and SMT solvers.
motivation: Cloud-based IoT access control configurations can have security vulnerabilities due to unintended information flow between devices, which is not captured by checking permissions in isolation.
method: The authors formally model AWS IoT Core components, define an information flow graph, and use an SMT solver to build a finite representation for verification, implemented in a tool called IOT:POKER.
result: The tool is assessed on a realistic scenario and several real-world policies, demonstrating its ability to identify potential information flow vulnerabilities.
conclusion: The approach provides a practical method for verifying information flow in IoT access control policies, but it is not related to quantum information or quantum systems.

title: Secure Aggregation For Privacy-Preserving Federated Learning On Clinical Eeg Data
authors: Mohsen Toorani Pouya Rajabi
abstract: ArXiv:2607.28191v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Federated learning enables multiple institutions to train shared models without exchanging raw clinical EEG data, but it does not fully prevent privacy leakage from individual model updates. This paper presents a privacy-preserving federated learning framework for clinical EEG data using masking-based secure aggregation as the core protection mechanism. The framework combines graph-based communication, threshold secret sharing, dropout-resilient aggregation, local update clipping, an optional Bloom filter-based privacy-preserving record-linkage initialization module, and auxiliary-notary-based verifiability. It supports both semi-honest and malicious aggregation settings and is implemented using the Flower federated learning framework. The secure-aggregation variants are evaluated in a simulated cross-silo healthcare setting using TUH EEG-derived data under different client configurations. Under the stated assumptions, the secure variants hide individual updates from the aggregation server. The results show that these variants remain compatible with federated model training, although malicious-setting safeguards and lightweight consistency-checking mechanisms introduce additional computation, communication, and round-duration overhead. The semi-honest variant provides the lowest overhead among the secure configurations, while malicious and auxiliary-notary variants offer stronger consistency, integrity, and lightweight verification support at higher cost.
tldr: This paper presents a privacy-preserving federated learning framework for clinical EEG data using secure aggregation, but it is not aligned with the specified research directions.
motivation: Federated learning for clinical EEG data risks privacy leakage from model updates, motivating the need for secure aggregation.
method: The framework uses masking-based secure aggregation, threshold secret sharing, dropout-resilient aggregation, and optional Bloom filter-based record linkage, implemented with Flower.
result: Secure variants hide individual updates from the server but introduce overhead; semi-honest variant has lowest overhead.
conclusion: The framework provides privacy-preserving federated learning for EEG data, but its focus is on applied machine learning and privacy, not quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Generalized Query-Oriented Image Semantic Coding Empowered By Large Ai Models And Semantic-Aware Hybrid Beamforming
authors: Vincent W. S. Wong Sin-Yu Huang
abstract: ArXiv:2607.28276v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Semantic communication is an emerging paradigm that can preserve the meaning of data during transmission. However, human users are often interested in specific semantic content based on their intent, and users' intent is often not considered in current semantic coding design. Moreover, most of the existing semantic models are fine-tuned using specific datasets, which limits their generalization capability. Furthermore, how to prioritize semantically important features in large-scale multiple-input multiple-output orthogonal frequency-division multiplexing (MIMO-OFDM) systems remains largely unexplored. To address the aforementioned challenges, in this paper, we propose a generalized query-oriented image semantic coding (QO-ISC) framework. In the proposed framework, the transmitter extracts features which are relevant to the user's query and the receiver reconstructs an image based on those features. We use a pretrained large artificial intelligence (AI) model (LAM) to enhance general feature representations. We develop a semantic-aware hybrid beamforming (SA-HBF) algorithm to prioritize semantically important features for large-scale MIMO-OFDM system. When evaluated on unseen object categories within the dataset, simulation results show that our proposed generalized QO-ISC framework achieves better performance than the traditional codec and two state-of-the-art semantic coding schemes.
tldr: This paper proposes a query-oriented image semantic coding framework using large AI models and semantic-aware hybrid beamforming for MIMO-OFDM systems.
motivation: Current semantic coding does not consider user intent, lacks generalization, and fails to prioritize semantically important features in large-scale MIMO-OFDM systems.
method: The framework extracts query-relevant features using a pretrained large AI model and employs a semantic-aware hybrid beamforming algorithm to prioritize important features.
result: Simulations on unseen object categories show the proposed framework outperforms traditional codecs and two state-of-the-art semantic coding schemes.
conclusion: The proposed approach improves semantic communication performance by incorporating user intent and semantic-aware beamforming.

title: The Capacity Of A Family Of Sticky Channels
authors: Mladen Kova\v{c}evi\'{c}
abstract: ArXiv:2607.28281v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We determine the capacity of a family of [MATH]-ary sticky-insertion channels. Fix [MATH] and [MATH], and let [MATH] be the unique positive solution of [MATH]. We prove that, for every repetition law supported on [MATH] and satisfying a coefficientwise-domination criterion with domination constant [MATH], the Shannon capacity equals the zero-error capacity, both being [MATH] bits per symbol. We also exhibit explicit repetition laws satisfying these conditions, one of which is given by the weighted Fuss--Catalan numbers. To the best of our knowledge, these are the first known cases of nontrivial repeat channels whose Shannon capacity has been determined exactly.
tldr: This paper determines the Shannon capacity of a family of sticky-insertion channels, showing it equals the zero-error capacity for certain repetition laws.
motivation: The capacity of insertion channels is a fundamental open problem in classical information theory, and this work provides exact results for a nontrivial family.
method: The authors prove that for repetition laws satisfying a coefficientwise-domination criterion, the Shannon capacity equals the zero-error capacity, and they exhibit explicit laws such as weighted Fuss-Catalan numbers.
result: They show that for these channels, both Shannon and zero-error capacities are equal to a specific value (log_2 of a root), providing the first exact capacity results for such repeat channels.
conclusion: This is a significant contribution to classical channel coding theory, but it is not related to quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid systems.

title: Low-Pathwidth Grand: Exact Likelihood-Ordered Enumeration For Bpsk Transmission Over Correlated Gaussian Noise
authors: Behrooz Razeghi
abstract: ArXiv:2607.28363v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The finite-block maximum-likelihood (ML) guarantee of soft-input GRAND requires querying noise-effect patterns in nonincreasing conditional-likelihood order. Under correlated Gaussian noise, additive reliability metrics and independent-block approximations need not preserve this order because the matched metric contains cross-coordinate interactions; the first codebook hit need not induce an ML codeword. We develop Low-Pathwidth GRAND (LP-GRAND) for binary phase-shift keying (BPSK) with precision matrix [MATH]. The candidate-dependent part of the Gaussian negative log-likelihood is an observation-dependent quadratic pseudo-Boolean energy whose interaction graph has edge [MATH] exactly when [MATH]. If [MATH] has half-bandwidth at most [MATH], this energy admits a trellis with at most [MATH] states per layer; a path decomposition of width [MATH] yields at most [MATH] bag assignments per layer. In real arithmetic, suffix dynamic programming and best-first complete-path enumeration enumerate patterns in nondecreasing energy. With complete enumeration and no abandonment, the first codebook hit induces an ML codeword for any nonempty binary codebook with equiprobable codewords. LP-GRAND agreed with exhaustive codeword ML in all [MATH] frames for two [MATH] codes. At nominal [MATH] dB, its empirical BLER was lower than that of each block-based approximation for six [MATH] codes.
tldr: This paper presents a novel algorithm for exact maximum-likelihood decoding of BPSK signals under correlated Gaussian noise using low-pathwidth trellis enumeration.
motivation: The paper addresses the problem of guaranteeing maximum-likelihood (ML) decoding in GRAND (Guessing Random Additive Noise Decoding) when noise is correlated, where standard reliability metrics fail to preserve likelihood order.
method: LP-GRAND constructs a trellis based on the precision matrix's half-bandwidth, enabling suffix dynamic programming and best-first enumeration of noise patterns in nondecreasing energy, ensuring the first codebook hit is ML.
result: LP-GRAND matched exhaustive ML decoding in all tested frames and achieved lower BLER than block-based approximations for several codes at nominal SNR.
conclusion: The algorithm provides an exact and efficient ML decoding method for correlated Gaussian noise, with potential applications in communication systems.

title: New Techniques For High-resolution Imaging And High-precision Wavefront Sensing Via Masked-aperture Interferometry
authors: Nithyanandan Thyagarajan, Bojan Nikolic, Chris Carilli, Laura Torino, Ubaldo Iriso
abstract: ArXiv:2607.27347v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Achieving high-angular-resolution imaging on subarcsecond scales is fundamentally limited by wavefront aberrations imparted by the propagation medium and by optical elements along the light path. Accurate recovery of source structure at these fine angular scales therefore relies on precise, real-time sensing and correction of wavefront aberrations. Drawing inspiration from radio interferometry, we have developed different approaches using masked apertures that directly measure both the amplitude and phase of the distortions to the electromagnetic wavefront while simultaneously reconstructing the underlying source structure. First is radio interferometry style self-calibration which can recover the complex electric field aberrations across the aperture with subarcsecond phase accuracy, equivalent to nanometer-level precision in optical pathlength, and simultaneously reconstruct the source structure with milliarcsecond (sub-micron) accuracy. Second is closure invariant-based source reconstruction which allows to bypass self-calibration and errors therein entirely while achieving comparable fidelity in the recovered source structure. These methods have been validated on the ALBA synchrotron beamline. Together, these methods provide a reliable framework for nanometre-scale high-precision wavefront sensing and subarcsecond-scale high angular resolution imaging, enabling new possibilities for masked-aperture interferometry. Potential applications span laboratory and synchrotron facilities to astronomy, including beam diagnostics in the Large Hadron Collider and masked-aperture interferometry on space telescopes such as the James Webb Space Telescope.
tldr: This paper presents new techniques for high-resolution imaging and wavefront sensing using masked-aperture interferometry, validated on a synchrotron beamline.
motivation: To overcome wavefront aberrations that limit subarcsecond imaging, the authors aim to develop methods that simultaneously sense wavefront errors and reconstruct source structure.
method: They adapt radio interferometry techniques, including self-calibration and closure invariants, to masked-aperture interferometry, measuring amplitude and phase distortions.
result: The methods achieve nanometer-level wavefront sensing precision and milliarcsecond imaging accuracy, validated on the ALBA synchrotron beamline.
conclusion: The framework enables high-precision wavefront sensing and high-resolution imaging, with potential applications in astronomy and beam diagnostics.

title: Vector Field Theory In Motion: Revealing Latent Potentials In Soccer Dynamics
authors: Paula Rodr\'iguez-S\'anchez, Roberto L\'opez Del Campo, Ricardo Resta, Jos\'e J. Ramasco, Javier M. Buld\'u, Johann H. Mart\'inez
abstract: ArXiv:2607.27838v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Team sports offer a natural laboratory for studying collective motion in competitive environments. While recent tracking technologies enabled detailed analysis of player and ball trajectories, most existing approaches rely on discrete events and local kinematic descriptors. This limits the possibility of studying team collective behavior. Here we introduce a physics-based framework to characterize collective dynamics using empirically reconstructed velocity vector fields defined over the pitch. Taking soccer as a paradigmatic example, we show that both ball and player movements generate smooth, predominantly irrotational vector fields. Each of these fields is generated by a potential providing compact, physically interpretable representations of collective motion and encoding how teams control, or constrain play across space during attacking and defensive phases in each match. Applied to an entire season of top-level competition, the resulting potentials reveal stable team-specific fingerprints and quantitative associations between potential gradients and effective ball progression.
tldr: This paper applies physics-based vector field analysis to soccer dynamics, revealing latent potentials that characterize team collective motion.
motivation: Existing sports analytics rely on discrete events and local kinematics, limiting the study of collective team behavior. The authors aim to provide a compact, physically interpretable representation of team dynamics.
method: They reconstruct velocity vector fields from player and ball trajectories, show they are predominantly irrotational, and derive scalar potentials. They analyze an entire season of top-level soccer to extract team-specific fingerprints and relate potential gradients to ball progression.
result: The potentials reveal stable team-specific patterns and quantitative associations between potential gradients and effective ball progression.
conclusion: The framework offers a novel way to characterize collective motion in team sports, but it is not related to quantum information, thermodynamics, quantum networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: Dynamical Low-Rank Filters For Data Assimilation
authors: Yoshihito Kazashi, Youssef Marzouk, Fabio Nobile, Fabio Zoccolan
abstract: ArXiv:2607.27432v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We propose dynamical low-rank (DLR) type filters for data-assimilation problems based on stochastic differential equations (SDEs). In detail, first we derive a DLRA filter for minimizing jointly the mean and covariance error, as well as a strategy to efficiently include the relevant orthogonal directions. This last approach allows the main subspace to evolve also according to the observation operator. Those procedures naturally extend to a Kalman-Bucy type filter when dealing with linear drift, and to ensemble methods, too, resulting also suitable for problems described by nonlinear drift and possible non-Gaussian distribution. Moreover, we further propose a preliminary particle-type DLRA filter that shows potentiality in nonlinear settings. Numerical simulations show the efficacy of these procedures in relevant applications, opening up to further studies in these filtering directions.
tldr: This paper proposes dynamical low-rank filters for data assimilation in stochastic differential equations, focusing on computational efficiency for high-dimensional state estimation.
motivation: Data assimilation in high-dimensional systems is computationally challenging; low-rank approximations can reduce cost while maintaining accuracy.
method: The authors derive dynamical low-rank approximation (DLRA) filters that minimize mean and covariance error, incorporate observation directions, and extend to Kalman-Bucy and ensemble methods, plus a particle-type filter.
result: Numerical simulations demonstrate efficacy in relevant applications, showing improved performance and scalability.
conclusion: The proposed filters offer promising tools for data assimilation, opening avenues for further research in filtering and uncertainty quantification.

title: Adaptive Security At The Edge For 6G-Enabled Healthcare IoT
authors: Ijaz Ahmad, Ijaz Ahmad, Erkki Harjula
abstract: ArXiv:2607.27858v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Healthcare IoT services increasingly rely on edge gateways to relay routine telemetry and deliver rare but timecritical alarms. Even short traffic bursts can inflate worstcase delay and interfere with urgent messages. We present NANOEDGEGUARD, a kernel-plane closed-loop controller that observes per-source traffic intensity at the edge and enforces an auditable, multi-tier rate policy using in-kernel traffic-control hooks. Unlike static firewall rules or user-space control loops, our design prioritizes fast actuation and explicit recovery through hysteresis, and it records policy transitions for auditability. Using a Raspberry Pi gateway hosting an MQTT broker and two ESP32 endpoints generating vitals, alarms, and a timed burst, we show that adaptive kernel-plane rate control reduces the 99th-percentile alarm RTT by 13.3% compared to a user-space firewall baseline while maintaining no-enforcement-level RTT, and it reduces excess admitted burst traffic by 46% compared to no enforcement. These early results indicate that adaptive, auditable enforcement at the gateway can improve resilience for healthcare IoT, and it can be extended toward on-demand policy deployment in future edge intelligence.
tldr: This paper presents a kernel-plane adaptive rate control system for healthcare IoT edge gateways, focusing on network traffic management rather than quantum information.
motivation: Healthcare IoT edge gateways need to handle traffic bursts to ensure timely delivery of critical alarms, but static rules and user-space controls are insufficient.
method: The authors implement NANOEDGEGUARD, a closed-loop controller in the kernel plane that monitors per-source traffic and enforces multi-tier rate policies with hysteresis, using Linux traffic-control hooks.
result: Experiments on a Raspberry Pi gateway with MQTT and ESP32 endpoints show a 13.3% reduction in 99th-percentile alarm RTT and a 46% reduction in excess burst traffic compared to baselines.
conclusion: Adaptive kernel-plane enforcement improves resilience for healthcare IoT and can be extended for on-demand policy deployment in edge intelligence.

title: Security Of World-Model-Based Embodied Ai: A Lifecycle Of Threats, Defenses, And Evaluation
authors: Fazhong Liu, Zhuoyan Chen, Haozhen Tan, Yan Meng, Guoxing Chen, Haojin Zhu
abstract: ArXiv:2607.28226v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: World models give embodied AI a predictive core: they compress observations into states, simulate action-conditioned futures, and enable planning beyond reactive control. This predictive layer, however, opens a new security boundary-compromise can propagate from data, sensors, prompts, or feedback into physical action. Rather than treating world models as an isolated component, this survey traces threats across their entire lifecycle-from data construction and representation learning, through state grounding and imagination, to trajectory evaluation, execution, and long-term adaptation via memory and tools. We show that familiar attack families: poisoning, backdoors, adversarial examples, sensor spoofing, prompt injection, trajectory manipulation, and supply-chain attacks take on distinct meanings when they corrupt world states, learned dynamics, affordance estimates, or safety costs. We also highlight a duality: world models can serve as runtime safety shields, yet when compromised or over-trusted they generate predictive safety illusions. The survey offers a lifecycle taxonomy, maps existing attacks to world-model security properties, outlines evaluation protocols for safety failures, and structures defenses across provenance, robust grounding, uncertainty-aware prediction, trajectory gating, feedback auditing, and deployment assurance.
tldr: A survey on security threats and defenses for world-model-based embodied AI, covering the full lifecycle from data to deployment.
motivation: World models in embodied AI introduce new security vulnerabilities that can propagate to physical actions, yet no comprehensive framework exists.
method: The paper proposes a lifecycle taxonomy, maps attack families to world-model components, and outlines defenses and evaluation protocols.
result: Identifies distinct security implications for world states, dynamics, affordances, and safety costs, and highlights the duality of world models as safety shields or sources of illusions.
conclusion: Calls for a lifecycle-aware security approach and structured defenses to mitigate risks in embodied AI systems.

title: Breaking Scale Separation In Metamaterials' Homogenization: Interface-Inertia-Enhanced Relaxed Micromorphic Model
authors: Angela Madeo, Leonardo Perez, Mohammad Sarhil
abstract: ArXiv:2607.27385v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Homogenized continuum models are widely used to describe wave propagation and band-gap behavior in mechanical metamaterials without explicitly resolving their microstructure. Their validity, however, typically relies on the classical separation of scales assumption, according to which the wavelength of the propagating disturbance is much larger than the characteristic size of the unit cell. In finite-size metamaterial samples and at higher frequencies, this assumption progressively breaks down, and the dynamic response becomes strongly influenced by the way the microstructure is truncated at the external boundaries. In this work we introduce a fundamentally new concept in the homogenized description of mechanical metamaterials: the inertial contribution of macroscopic interfaces. We show that different truncations of the same lattice generate boundaries with distinct mass distributions, which lead to measurable differences in the dynamic response of finite-sized specimens. To capture this complex mechanism in a homogenized framework, we extend the relaxed micromorphic model by introducing a kinetic surface energy defined on the boundary of the considered body. This generates an additional inertial term in the boundary conditions that can be seen as the homogenized counterpart of the interface inertia produced by the truncation of the microstructure. As a result, the homogenized model can now distinguish between finite-sized specimens that share identical bulk properties but differ only in the configuration of their interfaces. The proposed formulation preserves the variational structure of the relaxed micromorphic model while enabling the continuum to reproduce boundary-dependent responses observed in fully resolved simulations, particularly in frequency regimes ....... See the PDF for the full abstract.
tldr: This paper introduces a relaxed micromorphic model with interface inertia to capture boundary effects in metamaterial homogenization, but it is unrelated to quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems.
motivation: The authors aim to address the breakdown of scale separation in metamaterial homogenization, where finite-size effects and boundary truncations affect dynamic response.
method: They extend the relaxed micromorphic model by adding a kinetic surface energy on boundaries, introducing an inertial term in boundary conditions to represent interface inertia from microstructure truncation.
result: The enhanced model can distinguish finite specimens with identical bulk properties but different interface configurations, reproducing boundary-dependent responses in frequency regimes where classical homogenization fails.
conclusion: The proposed formulation preserves variational structure while capturing interface inertia effects, offering a more accurate homogenized description for finite metamaterial samples.

title: Discrete To Continuum Limits In Bayesian Inverse Problems
authors: Alexander Katsevich
abstract: ArXiv:2607.27408v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We develop a posterior-level discrete-to-continuum theory for Bayesian inverse problems whose finite-dimensional priors arise from local finite-difference regularization and whose likelihoods are of a general convex GLM-type form. In contrast to continuum-first approaches, the continuum prior and posterior are not assumed at the outset but are constructed as limits of the finite-dimensional probability measures used in numerical computation. First, with the total information parameter [MATH] and the regularization strength [MATH] fixed, we prove weak convergence on [MATH] of the reconstructed discrete Gaussian priors and posterior measures to well-defined continuum laws. We then consider a coupled grid-refinement and small-noise limit in which [MATH] and [MATH], while [MATH] remains fixed. Under explicit growth conditions relating [MATH] and [MATH], we prove that the reconstructed discrete MAP estimates converge to the unique minimizer [MATH] of the limiting continuum cost functional, that the reconstructed posterior measures concentrate at [MATH], and that their centered and rescaled fluctuations converge to [MATH], where [MATH] is the Hessian of the continuum cost functional at [MATH]. Finally, we show that the same deterministic limit and Gaussian fluctuation law are obtained by first constructing the continuum posterior and then taking its small-noise, high-regularization limit.
tldr: This paper develops a discrete-to-continuum limit theory for Bayesian inverse problems with finite-difference priors, proving convergence of posterior measures and MAP estimates.
motivation: To rigorously justify the use of finite-dimensional approximations in Bayesian inverse problems by showing that discrete priors and posteriors converge to well-defined continuum limits.
method: The authors analyze finite-dimensional Gaussian priors from local finite-difference regularization and general convex GLM-type likelihoods, proving weak convergence of measures and deriving asymptotic limits under coupled grid-refinement and small-noise scaling.
result: They establish weak convergence of discrete priors and posteriors to continuum laws, and show that MAP estimates converge to the minimizer of a continuum cost functional with Gaussian fluctuations governed by its Hessian.
conclusion: The work provides a posterior-level discrete-to-continuum theory that justifies numerical approaches and yields the same limits as continuum-first methods.

title: Comparison Of A Parametric Physics-Informed Neural Network And A Tensorial Reduced-Order Model For The Shallow-Water Dam-Break Problem
authors: Anton Myshak, Md Rezwan Bin Mizan, Ilya Timofeyev
abstract: ArXiv:2607.27433v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We develop two parametric data-driven reduced models: a physics-informed neural network (PINN) and a non-intrusive tensorial reduced-order model (TROM), and apply both approaches to the parametrized one-dimensional shallow-water dam-break problem. Both reduced models do not require time integration and learn a direct solution map from space, time, and dam-break parameters to the physical state. We present a detailed comparison for out-of-sample and extrapolated parameter values. In addition, we demonstrate that it is essential to introduce shock-aware collocation to improve the robustness of the PINN model.
tldr: This paper compares a physics-informed neural network and a tensorial reduced-order model for the shallow-water dam-break problem, focusing on computational efficiency and accuracy.
motivation: The authors aim to develop efficient parametric reduced-order models for the shallow-water dam-break problem, which is relevant to fluid dynamics and engineering applications.
method: They implement a physics-informed neural network (PINN) and a non-intrusive tensorial reduced-order model (TROM), both learning a direct map from parameters to the solution without time integration, and introduce shock-aware collocation for the PINN.
result: The comparison shows that both models can approximate the solution, but the PINN requires shock-aware collocation for robustness, and TROM performs better for extrapolated parameters.
conclusion: The paper concludes that TROM is more robust for extrapolation, while PINN benefits from specialized training, but the work is primarily in computational fluid dynamics and not aligned with the user's quantum information research interests.

title: Dynamical Low-Rank Smoothing
authors: Youssef Marzouk, Fabio Nobile, Fabio Zoccolan
abstract: ArXiv:2607.27438v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Computational costs often make smoothing procedures prohibitive for high-dimensional data assimilation problems. To address this challenge, we propose a dynamical low-rank approximation (DLRA) methodology for smoothing concerning frameworks based on stochastic differential equations. We extend the previously developed joint mean-and-covariance optimization (JMCO) filtering setting to derive a reduced-order smoother via the Rauch--Tung--Striebel recursion and establish the corresponding Kalman--Bucy smoothing for affine drift dynamics. The resulting algorithms retain the adaptive nature of DLRA while significantly reducing the computational time and storage of the whole smoothing procedure.
tldr: This paper proposes a dynamical low-rank approximation method for smoothing in high-dimensional data assimilation, extending filtering techniques to reduce computational cost.
motivation: Smoothing procedures are computationally prohibitive for high-dimensional data assimilation problems, and existing methods are too expensive.
method: The authors extend the joint mean-and-covariance optimization (JMCO) filtering setting to derive a reduced-order smoother via the Rauch-Tung-Striebel recursion, and establish Kalman-Bucy smoothing for affine drift dynamics using dynamical low-rank approximation.
result: The resulting algorithms retain the adaptive nature of DLRA while significantly reducing computational time and storage of the smoothing procedure.
conclusion: The proposed dynamical low-rank smoothing offers an efficient approach for high-dimensional data assimilation, but it is not related to quantum information or quantum thermodynamics.

title: Residual-Driven Lifting Identification For Nonlinear-Manifold Reduced-Order Models Of Parametrized Linear PDEs
authors: Francesco A. B. Silva, Jean C. Ragusa, Theron Guo, Rudy Geelen
abstract: ArXiv:2607.27471v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We introduce a residual-driven procedure for training nonlinear-manifold reduced-order models for parametrized linear partial differential equations that, given prescribed latent and lifting spaces, identifies the nonlinear lifting without high-fidelity solution snapshots. The approximation is represented by a low-dimensional latent coordinate together with a nonlinear lifting into a richer reduced space. Rather than fitting the lifting to snapshot data, we determine it by minimizing a computable residual-based upper bound for the state error. For affinely parametrized operators, the resulting training objective admits an efficient offline--online decomposition, and the lifting update reduces to a sequence of low-dimensional weighted least-squares problems. Numerical evaluations on an advection--diffusion problem and a plane-strain elasticity benchmark show that the proposed approach substantially improves accuracy over linear subspaces. The resulting nonlinear models achieve accuracy comparable to snapshot-driven nonlinear-manifold training while avoiding high-fidelity snapshots in the lifting-identification stage.
tldr: This paper introduces a residual-driven method for training nonlinear-manifold reduced-order models for parametrized linear PDEs, focusing on computational efficiency and accuracy.
motivation: The paper aims to improve reduced-order modeling for parametrized PDEs by avoiding the need for high-fidelity snapshots when identifying nonlinear liftings.
method: The method minimizes a residual-based upper bound for the state error to determine the nonlinear lifting, with an efficient offline-online decomposition for affinely parametrized operators.
result: Numerical tests on advection-diffusion and elasticity problems show improved accuracy over linear subspaces and comparable performance to snapshot-driven methods.
conclusion: The proposed approach offers a snapshot-free alternative for nonlinear-manifold reduced-order models, achieving high accuracy with reduced computational cost.

title: Polynomial Maps Which Are Not Good For Nice Recurrence And Applications
authors: Rigoberto Zelada
abstract: ArXiv:2607.27582v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let [MATH] be the finite field with two elements and let [MATH] denote the countably infinite-dimensional vector space over [MATH]. We show that, unlike the case of polynomial maps [MATH] vanishing at zero which are always good for nice recurrence, there are polynomials [MATH] with [MATH] which fail to have this property. This disproves a conjecture of Bergelson and McCutcheon (c. 2000), which predicted that for any countably infinite abelian groups [MATH] and [MATH], every polynomial map [MATH] with [MATH] is good for nice recurrence. Moreover, we develop a dynamical mechanism which shows that the magnitude of intersections along polynomial paths is degree-sensitive (even when one considers only weakly mixing systems). Among other things, we also show that the Furstenberg-Sarkozy theorem for [MATH]-valued polynomials of degree at most [MATH] vanishing at zero is equivalent to a [MATH]-dimensional symmetric-difference weakening of the density polynomial Hales-Jewett conjecture. Thus, as we explain in detail in this paper, our observations not only shed new light on the phenomenon of polynomial recurrence but also constrain possible strategies for proving or disproving the density polynomial Hales-Jewett conjecture.
tldr: This paper disproves a conjecture about polynomial maps being good for nice recurrence in ergodic theory, with implications for the density polynomial Hales-Jewett conjecture.
motivation: The authors aim to resolve a conjecture by Bergelson and McCutcheon regarding polynomial recurrence in countable abelian groups, and to explore connections to combinatorial number theory.
method: They construct explicit polynomial maps over the finite field with two elements that fail the nice recurrence property, and develop a dynamical mechanism to show degree-sensitivity of intersections.
result: They disprove the conjecture and show that the Furstenberg-Sarkozy theorem for certain polynomials is equivalent to a weakening of the density polynomial Hales-Jewett conjecture.
conclusion: The findings constrain possible approaches to the density polynomial Hales-Jewett conjecture and deepen understanding of polynomial recurrence.

title: A Spectral-compensated Scheme For Space-parameter Poisson Noise Functionals: Error Bounds And Complexity Estimates
authors: Yun-Ching Chang
abstract: ArXiv:2607.27657v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This paper computes Poisson space noise functionals, [MATH], realised in a Gel'fand triple built from a L\'evy measure [MATH]. We isolate three discretisation parameters: a small-amplitude cut-off, a Donsker delta truncation M, and a chaos order N. For a stable-type intensity [MATH] ([MATH]), replacing discarded small amplitudes with matched Gaussian space noise improves the Wasserstein-1 error from [MATH] to [MATH]. The residual is asymptotically normal at [MATH]. This compensation reduces computational complexity from [MATH] to [MATH]. We also evaluate the Gamma-type boundary ([MATH]) and exponential tempering. Truncations converge algebraically (M) and super-geometrically (N). All predicted rates are tightly confirmed by deterministic numerical experiments via Gil-Pelaez inversion, eliminating Monte Carlo noise.
tldr: This paper develops a spectral-compensated scheme for computing Poisson space noise functionals, focusing on error bounds and complexity estimates.
motivation: The research interests focus on quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, and hybrid systems, none of which relate to stochastic analysis or Poisson noise functionals.
method: The method involves discretizing Poisson space noise with three parameters (amplitude cut-off, Donsker delta truncation, chaos order) and replacing discarded small amplitudes with matched Gaussian noise.
result: The compensation improves Wasserstein-1 error and reduces computational complexity, with asymptotic normality of the residual.
conclusion: The paper is purely mathematical/stochastic and has no connection to the specified research directions.

title: An Asymptotic-Preserving Dynamical Low-Rank Semi-Lagrangian Method For Multiscale Linear Kinetic Transport Equations
authors: Shun Li, Yan Jiang, Mengping Zhang, Tao Xiong
abstract: ArXiv:2607.27736v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this paper, we develop an asymptotic-preserving (AP) dynamical low-rank semi-Lagrangian method for multiscale linear kinetic transport equations. The method combines the large-time-step capability of semi-Lagrangian discretizations with the storage and cost reduction provided by low-rank representations. The proposed scheme couples an approximate macroscopic density update with the basis update Galerkin integrator for the kinetic distribution. To retain the reduced complexity in the semi-Lagrangian flux evaluation, the flux derivative is computed through a sampled angular quadrature strategy. We establish an unconditional stability analysis of the full-quadrature low-rank scheme in the constant-coefficient case. The error induced by angular sampling in the flux derivative is quantified. The resulting scheme is shown to be AP in the diffusive limit. Numerical experiments, including high-dimensional test cases, demonstrate that the proposed method is AP, stable under large time steps, and computationally efficient across kinetic and diffusive regimes.
tldr: This paper develops a numerical method for kinetic transport equations, which is unrelated to quantum information or quantum thermodynamics.
motivation: The paper aims to solve multiscale linear kinetic transport equations efficiently, which is a topic in computational physics and numerical analysis.
method: It combines asymptotic-preserving techniques with dynamical low-rank approximation and semi-Lagrangian discretization, using angular quadrature for flux evaluation.
result: The method is shown to be unconditionally stable in a constant-coefficient case, asymptotic-preserving in the diffusive limit, and efficient in numerical experiments.
conclusion: The proposed method offers a stable and efficient approach for multiscale kinetic transport problems, but it has no connection to the user's research interests.

title: A Unified Discrete Gradient-SAV Framework For Structure-Preserving Integration
authors: Elena Celledoni, David Mart\'in de Diego, Brynjulf Owren, Miguel Vaquero
abstract: ArXiv:2607.27795v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We present a framework combining discrete gradient (DG) methods with the Scalar Auxiliary Variable (SAV) approach to construct structure-preserving integrators for dissipative and conservative systems. The key observation is that SAV quadratization lifts the dynamics to an extended state space on which the modified energy has an exact discrete-gradient identity. This viewpoint yields three integrators with different accuracy and cost profiles: a first-order semi-implicit Forward Euler scheme, a second-order self-adjoint Midpoint scheme, and a second-order Predictive scheme with reduced implicitness. The construction extends to almost-Poisson systems and preserves selected Casimir invariants under an enforceable discrete condition. Numerical experiments cover the Allen--Cahn equation, an Ohta--Kawasaki-type nonlocal gradient flow, a double-well Hamiltonian oscillator, and a Poisson system with a nonlinear cubic Casimir.
tldr: This paper introduces a unified framework combining discrete gradient methods with scalar auxiliary variable (SAV) techniques for structure-preserving integration of dissipative and conservative systems.
motivation: The authors aim to develop numerical integrators that preserve geometric properties such as energy dissipation or conservation, which is important for long-time simulations of dynamical systems.
method: They propose a framework that lifts the dynamics to an extended state space via SAV quadratization, enabling an exact discrete-gradient identity for the modified energy. This yields three integrators: a first-order semi-implicit Forward Euler, a second-order self-adjoint Midpoint, and a second-order Predictive scheme.
result: The framework extends to almost-Poisson systems and preserves selected Casimir invariants under a discrete condition. Numerical experiments on Allen-Cahn, Ohta-Kawasaki, a double-well Hamiltonian oscillator, and a Poisson system demonstrate the method's effectiveness.
conclusion: The proposed unified DG-SAV framework provides a versatile approach for constructing structure-preserving integrators with varying accuracy and cost, applicable to a range of dissipative and conservative systems.

title: Dynamical Dimension And Shift Embeddability Without The Marker Property
authors: Ruxi Shi
abstract: ArXiv:2607.27880v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study the aperiodic inverse-limit system constructed in our earlier work as an example of a finite-mean-dimensional dynamical system without the marker property. We prove that its mean dimension and Meyerovitch's dynamical dimension are both equal to [MATH]. Despite the absence of the marker property, the system admits an equivariant topological embedding into the cubical shift with alphabet dimension [MATH]. As an auxiliary result, we prove that the dynamical dimension of the full shift over any compact metrizable alphabet is exactly the covering dimension of the alphabet, including when this dimension is infinite.
tldr: This paper studies mean dimension and dynamical dimension of a specific aperiodic inverse-limit system without the marker property, proving embedding into a cubical shift.
motivation: The paper aims to understand the relationship between mean dimension, dynamical dimension, and the marker property in topological dynamics.
method: The author analyzes the aperiodic inverse-limit system from prior work, proving equalities for mean dimension and dynamical dimension, and constructs an equivariant topological embedding into a cubical shift.
result: The mean dimension and dynamical dimension are both equal to a certain value, and the system embeds into a cubical shift with alphabet dimension equal to that value, despite lacking the marker property.
conclusion: The absence of the marker property does not preclude shift embeddability, and the dynamical dimension of full shifts equals the covering dimension of the alphabet.

title: OptGraph: Large Language Models Enhanced Evolutionary Optimization Via Graph Retrieval-Augmented Generation
authors: Xianchao Xiu, Jianhao Li, Huangyue Chen, Wanquan Liu
abstract: ArXiv:2607.27918v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Large language models (LLMs) have emerged as a powerful tool for automated evolutionary optimization, but existing methods remain limited in pattern reuse, error-aware refinement, and retrieval robustness across diverse tasks. To address these limitations, we propose OptGraph, the first optimization agentic workflow that introduces graph retrieval-augmented generation (GraphRAG). Specifically, OptGraph first constructs reusable experience as a typed graph, capturing the relationships among modeling patterns, problem formalization, implementation details, and error corrections. In the inference stage, OptGraph leverages graph neighborhood information to enrich retrieved knowledge, providing structured context to improve modeling, verification, and iterative refinement. Moreover, OptGraph supports adaptive knowledge updates, enabling the distillation of execution traces and verification feedback into reusable graph knowledge without ndertaking LLM parameter tuning. Extensive experiments on benchmark datasets show that our proposed OptGraph achieves an average exact accuracy 8.9% higher than the state-of-the-art prompt-based automated optimization frameworks. Our code has been made available at [URL].
tldr: This paper proposes OptGraph, an LLM-based evolutionary optimization framework enhanced with graph retrieval-augmented generation, but it is unrelated to quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems.
motivation: Existing LLM-based optimization methods lack pattern reuse, error-aware refinement, and retrieval robustness across tasks.
method: OptGraph constructs a typed graph of reusable experiences and uses graph neighborhood information to enrich retrieval, supporting adaptive knowledge updates without LLM parameter tuning.
result: Experiments show OptGraph achieves 8.9% higher average exact accuracy than state-of-the-art prompt-based optimization frameworks.
conclusion: GraphRAG can effectively enhance LLM-driven evolutionary optimization, but the work is outside the user's research scope.

title: Projective Norm-attainments And Their Implications
authors: Manwook Han, Sun Kwang Kim, Miguel Mart\'in, Abraham Rueda Zoca
abstract: ArXiv:2607.28054v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We show that nuclear norm-attaining operators (resp.\ polynomials) are always [MATH]-dense in the space of integral operators (resp.\ polynomials). Besides, the denseness is in norm if the predual space does not contain any isomorphic copy of [MATH]. We also show that there are reflexive spaces for which the set of projective norm-attaining elements does not coincide with the whole projective tensor product (which is indeed also reflexive here). Next, we show that if [MATH] is a II-polyhedral space, then every nuclear operator from an arbitrary space [MATH] to [MATH] attains its nuclear norm. As a consequence, if [MATH] or [MATH] has the approximation property, then the set of norm-attaining operators from [MATH] to [MATH] is dense. The argument extends to the multilinear and polynomial settings. Finally, we study proximinality results of a natural subspace of the projective tensor product and obtain an application to integral projective norm-attaining tensors which solves a proposed open question.
tldr: This paper studies projective norm-attaining operators and polynomials in Banach spaces, focusing on denseness and proximinality results.
motivation: The authors aim to understand when nuclear operators attain their nuclear norm and to solve an open question about integral projective norm-attaining tensors.
method: They use functional analysis techniques, including properties of projective tensor products, polyhedral spaces, and approximation properties.
result: They prove denseness of nuclear norm-attaining operators under certain conditions, show reflexive spaces where projective norm-attaining elements do not coincide with the whole tensor product, and solve an open question.
conclusion: The results contribute to the theory of norm-attainment in Banach spaces, but are not directly related to quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: From Lecture Notes To Lean: Formalizing A Textbook On Probability Theory
authors: Kenneth W. Shum Shuo Deng
abstract: ArXiv:2607.27298v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: As large language models become increasingly capable of generating mathematical arguments, mathematics is likely to face not a scarcity of proofs but an abundance of plausible ones. In such an environment, verification, exposition, and incorporation into reusable mathematical infrastructure become central tasks. We report on an ongoing Lean formalization of "Measure-Theoretic Probability: With Applications to Statistics, Finance, and Engineering", a fourteen-chapter upper-level undergraduate textbook covering topics from Riemann--Stieltjes integration to martingales and limit theorems. The project produces a machine-checked companion to the textbook and contributes reusable infrastructure for future formalizations involving probability theory. A Lean formalization provides computer-checked statements and proofs, makes hypotheses explicit, and allows readers to inspect the precise logical content of textbook results. A central challenge is to bridge textbook-facing statements with Mathlib's more general measure-theoretic interfaces. We reuse Mathlib results when possible and introduce reviewable interface lemmas when the textbook formulation and library abstraction differ. The project illustrates how formalized textbooks can support teaching, clarify mathematical assumptions, and help build the formal foundations needed for reliable AI-assisted mathematics.
tldr: This paper reports on the formalization of a probability theory textbook in the Lean proof assistant, focusing on verification and reusable infrastructure for AI-assisted mathematics.
motivation: With the rise of LLMs generating plausible but unverified mathematical arguments, there is a need for formal verification and reusable mathematical infrastructure.
method: The authors formalize chapters of a measure-theoretic probability textbook in Lean, bridging textbook statements with Mathlib's interfaces and introducing reviewable interface lemmas.
result: The project produces a machine-checked companion to the textbook and contributes reusable infrastructure for future formalizations in probability theory.
conclusion: Formalized textbooks can support teaching, clarify assumptions, and build foundations for reliable AI-assisted mathematics.

title: Extension Types For Free
authors: Nicolai Kraus
abstract: ArXiv:2607.27387v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Extension types are a concept in dependent type theory that has appeared in various contexts. The idea is to have types whose terms are partially determined, e.g. via a strict boundary condition. Standard examples are path types of cubical type theories (paths with fixed endpoints), Riehl and Shulman's name-giving extension types (terms fixed on subshapes), as well as the controlled-unfolding mechanism of cooltt and Agda (terms that are fixed if a condition is met). In each case, the type theory is equipped with a (meta-theoretic) face calculus, or shape layer, that governs their rules, and comes with intended semantics. We unify all these occurrences in a single framework where no new axioms or model constructions are needed, namely two-level type theory. This step, too, is free (semantically): the standard models of HoTT are automatically models of 2LTT, and the theory is conservative over HoTT. Extension types are definable, and the definition validates Riehl and Shulman's entire extension-type calculus: the rules hold strictly, and the postulated axioms, such as relative function extensionality, become theorems. In this way, every model of the base theory (HoTT) gives rise to a model of the same theory with extension types; the only genuine assumptions are which maps count as cofibrations. Conservativity makes the framework a tool for comparing type theories. We prove that cubical gluing, in a suitable formulation, is equivalent to univalence. On this basis, we suggest an approach toward the conjecture that cubical type theories are conservative over book HoTT, one of the central open problems of homotopy type theory. All results of the main body of the paper are auto-formalized in Agda --two-level, in a development that combines HoTT-internal arguments with reasoning that is external to HoTT.
tldr: This paper unifies various extension types in dependent type theory within two-level type theory, showing they are definable and conservative over HoTT.
motivation: Extension types appear in different type theories with ad-hoc rules; the author aims to provide a unified framework without new axioms.
method: The author uses two-level type theory (2LTT) to define extension types, proving that standard models of HoTT are models of 2LTT and that the theory is conservative over HoTT.
result: The paper shows that Riehl and Shulman's extension-type calculus holds strictly, relative function extensionality becomes a theorem, and cubical gluing is equivalent to univalence.
conclusion: The framework provides a tool for comparing type theories and suggests an approach to proving cubical type theories conservative over book HoTT.

title: Low-Latency Bootstrapping For Ckks Using Roots Of Unity
authors: Robin Koestler Jean-Sebastien Coron
abstract: ArXiv:2607.27401v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We introduce Sparse Roots of Unity (SPRU) bootstrapping, a new bootstrapping algorithm for the CKKS homomorphic encryption scheme for approximate arithmetic. The original CKKS bootstrapping method relies on homomorphically evaluating a polynomial that approximates modular reduction modulo q. In contrast, SPRU bootstrapping directly embeds the additive group modulo q into the complex roots of unity, which can be evaluated natively in the CKKS scheme. This approach significantly reduces the multiplicative depth required for bootstrapping, enabling the use of a smaller ring dimension and improving efficiency. In practice, using the OpenFHE C++ library, SPRU bootstrapping achieves up to a 5x reduction in latency when applied to ciphertexts with a small number of slots.
tldr: This paper introduces a new bootstrapping method for the CKKS homomorphic encryption scheme, reducing latency by using roots of unity.
motivation: The paper aims to improve the efficiency of CKKS bootstrapping, which is a critical operation in homomorphic encryption for approximate arithmetic.
method: The proposed SPRU bootstrapping embeds the additive group modulo q into complex roots of unity, natively evaluable in CKKS, reducing multiplicative depth and enabling smaller ring dimensions.
result: Using OpenFHE, SPRU bootstrapping achieves up to a 5x reduction in latency for ciphertexts with a small number of slots.
conclusion: The method offers a significant performance improvement for CKKS bootstrapping, particularly in low-latency scenarios.

title: Multi-Player Discrete-Bidding Games; Determinacy, Equilibria, And Complexity
authors: Fatima Murra Guy Avni
abstract: ArXiv:2607.27456v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Games on graphs constitute a fundamental model. Applications include reactive synthesis, which reduces to solving a zero-sum two-player game, and reasoning about multi-agent systems by modeling them as a multi-player game. We study a class of graph games called bidding games in which the players are allocated a budget, and in each turn, an auction determines which player moves the token. Two-player bidding games have been extensively studied. We study, for the first time, multi-player bidding games. We focus on discrete bidding, which imposes granularity restrictions on the players' budgets and bids. The original motivation for discrete bidding is practical applications, and technically, it is appealing that the game has only finitely-many configurations. We initiate our study by considering a game between two coalitions of players. We show that under mild assumptions on the mechanism that is applied to break bidding ties, bidding games are determined: from every initial configuration, one of the coalitions has a winning strategy. Thus, we identify a sub-class of multi-player concurrent games that is determined. We extend the result to existence of a value in mean-payoff games. Using determinacy, we show that a pure Nash equilibrium always exists in qualitative games. Finally, we show that the complexity of deciding which coalition wins from a given configuration is PSPACE-hard already in reachability games and already for budgets given in unary. This is in stark contrast to two-player games, which are known to be in NP and coNP even for budgets given in binary.
tldr: This paper studies multi-player bidding games on graphs, focusing on determinacy, equilibria, and computational complexity.
motivation: The authors aim to extend the study of two-player bidding games to the multi-player setting, which is relevant for modeling multi-agent systems.
method: They formalize multi-player discrete bidding games, consider coalitions, and analyze determinacy under tie-breaking assumptions, existence of pure Nash equilibria, and complexity of deciding the winner.
result: They show determinacy for coalition games, existence of pure Nash equilibria in qualitative games, and PSPACE-hardness for reachability games even with unary budgets.
conclusion: The paper provides foundational results for multi-player bidding games, but it is not related to quantum information, thermodynamics, quantum networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: Revisiting The Adversarial Robustness Of Graph-Based Traffic Forecasting
authors: Qingzhao Zhang
abstract: ArXiv:2607.27604v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Traffic forecasting by graph-based AI is a critical component of intelligent transportation systems, motivating security research on robustness to malicious sensor readings. We argue that prior robustness evaluations are largely shaped by unrealistic threat models and untargeted objectives, so both attacks and defenses must be revisited. We study a practical adversary with limited model knowledge and the ability to monitor and manipulate only a few road sensors. More importantly, practical attacks can be localized to specific links or routes, causing incorrect estimated arrival times or unnecessary rerouting while leaving the broader network largely unaffected. This targeted setting remains underexplored, and defenses such as adversarial training do not transfer well from the norm-bounded attacks they train on to structurally different, physics-aware attacks that mimic genuine congestion. We therefore reframe robustness as a detection problem, introducing a learned physics-informed detector whose output is fed to a hardened forecaster as an input feature and trained against adaptive attacks with the forecaster fixed. We evaluate across a variety of model architectures and benchmarks. The physics-aware attack multiplies target-link error several-fold while the network-wide error barely moves, and adversarial training, tuned to norm-bounded perturbations, barely dents it. Our detection--mitigation defense improves even on adversarial training hardened against the physics-aware attack itself, on [MATH] of [MATH] model--dataset settings and by the widest margin on a held-out attack, at near-zero clean cost. The results emphasize the need to examine abstracted AI adversarial attacks under application-specific constraints to assess their true security impacts.
tldr: This paper revisits adversarial robustness in graph-based traffic forecasting, proposing a physics-aware attack and a detection-mitigation defense.
motivation: Prior robustness evaluations of traffic forecasting models rely on unrealistic threat models and untargeted objectives, failing to capture practical attacks that can locally manipulate sensor readings.
method: The authors introduce a physics-aware attack that mimics genuine congestion and a learned physics-informed detector that feeds into a hardened forecaster, trained against adaptive attacks.
result: The physics-aware attack significantly increases target-link error while keeping network-wide error low, and adversarial training fails to defend against it; the proposed defense improves robustness across most settings.
conclusion: The study highlights the need to consider application-specific constraints in adversarial AI research, reframing robustness as a detection problem for traffic forecasting.

title: Charge: Leveraging Cwe Hierarchies For Hardware Security SystemVerilog Assertion Generation
authors: Cynthia Sturton Xiao Tan
abstract: ArXiv:2607.27776v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This paper presents CHARGE, an automated framework for generating security properties for unverified RTL modules using CWEs and large language models (LLMs). The hallmark is a reasoning process that leverages the hierarchical nature of CWE entries to improve accuracy when identifying security-critical assets in unverified RTL modules. As a result, the approach can infer expected security behaviors and generate properties from identified assets and CWE semantics, avoiding the need for trusted design specifications and reducing manual engineering effort. We evaluate the framework on the Hack@DAC18, 19, and 21 open source SoC designs using OpenAI's GPT-4.1. CHARGE detects 27 of 42 known bugs in these designs. For Hack@DAC21 OpenPiton SoC, 89% of the generated SVAs run in Cadence JasperGold FPV, and 92.2% are non-vacuous. We compare to an open-source, manually written set of properties for these designs and find that CHARGE correctly writes properties for three bugs in which the manually written properties were incorrect. In addition, CHARGE-generated properties identify a new bug in the Hack@DAC21 OpenPiton SoC that was not previously identified.
tldr: This paper presents CHARGE, an automated framework that uses CWE hierarchies and LLMs to generate security assertions for hardware RTL designs.
motivation: Hardware security verification is challenging and often requires manual effort; the authors aim to automate the generation of security properties without trusted specifications.
method: CHARGE leverages the hierarchical structure of CWE entries to identify security-critical assets in RTL modules, then uses LLMs to infer expected behaviors and generate SystemVerilog assertions.
result: On Hack@DAC18/19/21 designs, CHARGE detects 27 of 42 known bugs, with high non-vacuous assertion rates, and even finds a new bug in OpenPiton.
conclusion: The approach demonstrates that LLMs combined with CWE hierarchies can effectively automate hardware security property generation, reducing manual effort.

title: Safeguards Based On Copyable Context Cannot Provide Reliable Safety For LLMs
authors: Pingyu Wu, Lingyao Zhu, Weiming Zhang, Nenghai Yu
abstract: ArXiv:2607.27951v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Large language model safeguards decide whether to answer before seeing how an answer will be used. This creates a basic problem for dual-use tasks: the same answer can help an authorized professional or an attacker, while an attacker can imitate a benign request and interaction history. We separate the capability released by the model from the evidence available about downstream use. When that evidence is copyable, we derive the exact worst-case floor on attacker assistance while preserving useful answers. The result yields a safety trilemma: Useful Capability, Reliable Safety, and Open Access cannot coexist. We then show how a trusted credential can complement existing safeguards by adding hard-to-copy information that predicts actual downstream use, and identify the stronger condition needed to eliminate the floor. Evidence from dual-use evaluations, adaptive attacks, and deployed trusted-access programs supports the practical relevance of these conditions.
tldr: This paper analyzes the fundamental limits of LLM safeguards when context is copyable, proposing a trilemma and trusted credentials.
motivation: LLM safeguards cannot reliably distinguish benign from malicious uses of dual-use capabilities when attackers can imitate benign contexts.
method: The authors derive a worst-case floor on attacker assistance using copyable evidence, and propose trusted credentials as hard-to-copy evidence.
result: They establish a safety trilemma: Useful Capability, Reliable Safety, and Open Access cannot coexist, and identify conditions to eliminate the floor.
conclusion: Trusted credentials can complement safeguards but cannot fully resolve the trilemma; stronger conditions are needed.

title: Driving Up Inference Energy On SNNs: Per-Sample And Universal Sponge Attacks
authors: Haralampos-G. Stratigopoulos Spyridon Raptis
abstract: ArXiv:2607.27990v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Spiking Neural Networks (SNNs) communicate through sparse binary spike events rather than dense activations, enabling energy-efficient inference on neuromorphic hardware and motivating their use in always-on, battery-powered edge systems. We show that this same efficiency advantage creates a distinct security risk: sponge attacks can increase inference-time spike activity and synaptic workload, inflating energy consumption while remaining difficult to detect through correctness-based monitoring alone. Prior input-space efficiency attacks on SNNs have focused on per-sample optimization, primarily in rate-coded settings. We extend this threat to native event-based binary inputs and study two attack models. First, we develop a per-sample sponge attack that crafts a custom adversarial spike train for each input via gradient-based optimization. This attack increases per-inference SynOps by 1.5-2.6x on three SNN models for the NMNIST, SHD, and IBM DVS Gesture datasets, while preserving the predicted class on at least 98% of evaluated samples. Second, to the best of our knowledge, we introduce the first universal sponge attack for native event-based SNN inputs: a fixed binary perturbation computed offline and applied via XOR to all subsequent inputs. Although weaker, it still inflates SynOps by 1.09-1.24x across all three datasets and represents a more realistic deployment threat because it requires no per-input optimization. Mapping SynOp inflation to estimated Loihi-1 energy yields per-inference overheads from 14 [MATH]J to 13.24 mJ. These results show that native event-based SNNs are vulnerable to practical input-space efficiency attacks, and that reusable universal perturbations can accumulate into meaningful battery drain in continuously deployed edge systems.
tldr: This paper studies sponge attacks on spiking neural networks to increase energy consumption, which is unrelated to the user's research interests in quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid systems.
motivation: The user's research interests focus on quantum information theory, information thermodynamics, quantum networks, and hybrid quantum systems. This paper is about adversarial attacks on neuromorphic hardware, which is a classical machine learning security topic.
method: The authors develop per-sample and universal sponge attacks that craft adversarial spike trains to inflate synaptic operations (SynOps) in SNNs, using gradient-based optimization and binary perturbations.
result: The per-sample attack increases SynOps by 1.5-2.6x, and the universal attack by 1.09-1.24x, across three datasets, with estimated energy overheads up to 13.24 mJ per inference.
conclusion: The paper concludes that SNNs are vulnerable to energy-based attacks, but this has no connection to quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Optimal PSPACE-hardness Of Approximating $q$-CSP Reconfiguration
authors: Naoto Ohsaka Shuichi Hirahara
abstract: ArXiv:2607.28099v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In the Maxmin [MATH]-CSP Reconfiguration problem, given a satisfiable [MATH]-CSP instance and a pair of its satisfying assignments, we are asked to transform one assignment into the other by repeatedly changing the value assigned to a single variable. The objective is to find such a transformation that maximizes the minimum fraction of satisfied constraints along the transformation. In this paper, we prove that for any [MATH] and [MATH], Maxmin [MATH]-CSP Reconfiguration is [MATH]-hard to approximate within a factor of [MATH]. To complement this hardness result, we prove that a [MATH]-factor approximation for Maxmin [MATH]-CSP Reconfiguration is in [MATH] in the perfect completeness case. These results establish the optimal [MATH]-hardness of approximating Maxmin [MATH]-CSP Reconfiguration for every [MATH] under [MATH].

title: Learning To Persuade Privately Informed Receivers

We design a learning algorithm that achieves regret [MATH] relative to the optimal scheme of a sender who knows the private signaling scheme of the receiver, with polynomial dependence on the sizes of the state space and the receiver's signal alphabet. title: Exact Total Variation Minimizers As Non-Oscillatory Limiters In High-Order Methods For Conservation Laws
authors: Gabriel P. Langlois, Jerome Darbon, Rongjie Lai, Chi-Wang Shu, Xiangxiong Zhang
abstract: ArXiv:2607.27416v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: High-order numerical methods for conservation laws can generate spurious oscillations near discontinuities. We propose to suppress these oscillations by post-processing the numerical solution with a total variation (TV) denoising step that reduces the total variation of the nodal values. For a general analysis operator, the resulting discrete minimization problem need not satisfy the submodularity property that existing exact max-flow algorithms require, so we instead compute the TV minimizer exactly using a differential inclusion algorithm. In one dimension, the differential inclusion algorithm computes the TV minimizer in finitely many steps, requires no tuning of algorithmic parameters, and preserves the total mass. In two dimensions, we apply the 1D algorithm dimension by dimension. We test the method as a post-processing limiter for Fourier pseudospectral methods and a fifth-order finite difference scheme applied to scalar conservation laws, compressible Euler equations, and the two-dimensional incompressible Euler equations.
tldr: This paper proposes a total variation denoising post-processing method to suppress oscillations in high-order numerical methods for conservation laws.
motivation: High-order numerical methods for conservation laws can produce spurious oscillations near discontinuities, which need to be suppressed.

result: The method is tested on Fourier pseudospectral and fifth-order finite difference schemes for scalar conservation laws and Euler equations, showing effectiveness in reducing oscillations.
conclusion: The proposed TV limiter provides a parameter-free, mass-conserving approach to control oscillations in high-order methods.

title: Sharp Cyclicity Of Neutral Entry--Exit Cycles With Quadratic Grazing
authors: Haibo Lu
abstract: ArXiv:2607.27464v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We determine how many limit cycles can bifurcate when an invariant-line entry--exit delay and a quadratic grazing of the switching line occur in the same planar slow--fast return circuit. We consider continuous piecewise-smooth systems in which these mechanisms are separated by regular flow segments. For positive [MATH], the physical local cyclicity is at most two when the smooth-reference curvature and leading grazing-mismatch coefficient have the same sign, and at most three when their signs are opposite. Under a rank-two unfolding, the applicable bound is attained in each sign class for every sufficiently small fixed positive singular parameter. To prove these statements, we derive, to every prescribed finite order near a balanced neutral cycle, a parameter-uniform Poincar\'e displacement expansion and the one-sided derivative estimates required for zero counting. Its leading nonsmooth contribution is the classical three-halves grazing term, whose coefficient is given explicitly by contact, branch-mismatch, and global-transmission data. A polynomial family realizes both sign cases. We also construct a qualitatively admissible quartic extension of a published cutoff Gause predator--prey model, with its decisive curvature and rank conditions certified by interval arithmetic. Our contribution is the sign-sharp, parameter-uniform composition of the classical grazing law with an entry--exit passage at unit multiplier.

motivation: The paper aims to determine the maximum number of limit cycles that can bifurcate in a specific planar slow-fast return circuit combining an invariant-line entry-exit delay and quadratic grazing.
method: The authors derive parameter-uniform Poincaré displacement expansions and one-sided derivative estimates, using the classical three-halves grazing term and interval arithmetic for certification.
result: They show that the local cyclicity is at most two or three depending on sign conditions, and that these bounds are attained under rank-two unfolding.
conclusion: The work provides a sign-sharp, parameter-uniform composition of grazing and entry-exit passage, but it is not related to quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: Puncture-Forgetting Maps For Measured Foliations And Applications In Teichm\"uller Space And Complex Dynamics
authors: Insung Park Jeremy Kahn
abstract: ArXiv:2607.27552v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We introduce puncture-forgetting maps for measured foliations and investigate their relations with mapping class groups, Teichm\"uller spaces, and extremal length. To this end, we develop the notions of cube complexes of pre-homotopic multicurves and tree coordinate systems on CAT(0) cube complexes. As an application to the dynamics of post-critically finite rational maps on the Riemann sphere, we obtain a partial result toward the finite curve attractor conjecture posed by Kevin Pilgrim. We also apply these methods to uncover a relation between horospheres and geodesic flows in the universal curve over Teichm\"uller space.

title: A Novel Sampling Method For Reconstruction Of A Moving Point Acoustic Source In $\mathbb{R}^3$
authors: Guanqiu Ma, Shuang Li, Hongxia Guo
abstract: ArXiv:2607.27621v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this paper, we introduce a novel sampling method to recovering the trajectory of a moving point source in R^3, where both the spatial location and emission moment of the moving point source are unknown. Combining algebraic theory with geometric knowledge, we prove the uniqueness of the source location by using measured data from five observation points. Our sampling method constructs an indicator function based on the property that the residual of the time difference of arrival constraint formula vanishes at the true source location. It achieves the reconstruction of the spatial positions and emission moments of a moving point source only using data from five observation points and their corresponding arrival times. The algorithm not only reduces the required number of observation points, but also improves computational efficiency, stability, and noise resistance. Numerical experiments verify the effectiveness of the method.
tldr: This paper introduces a novel sampling method for reconstructing the trajectory of a moving point acoustic source in 3D space using only five observation points.
motivation: The authors aim to reduce the number of observation points required for source localization while improving computational efficiency and noise resistance.
method: They combine algebraic theory and geometric knowledge to prove uniqueness of the source location, and construct an indicator function based on the residual of the time difference of arrival constraint.
result: The method reconstructs spatial positions and emission moments using only five observation points, with numerical experiments demonstrating effectiveness.
conclusion: The proposed method offers a more efficient and stable approach to moving acoustic source reconstruction.
